opening.headline: After changing the prompt, if quality drops significantly and the issue cannot be prevented, the design blocks the promotion itself by integrating it into the evaluation gate and scorer.
body: On Friday afternoon, we changed one line of the prompt and immediately deployed it to production. By Monday, user complaints had accumulated and response quality metrics had significantly degraded. The code was functioning correctly, so the deployment pipeline generated no warnings.

The issue was that there was no gate in the pipeline to block changes that failed quality standards. In this lesson, you will learn about evaluation gates that changes must pass before moving to the next environment, scoring mechanisms to assess outputs, and thresholds to define pass/fail criteria. We will then examine where gates fit into the deployment flow of Declarative Automation Bundles and explore cases where operational deployments are halted when thresholds are not met.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Explain the meaning of evaluation gate, scorer, and threshold value.
Evaluation results that need to prevent promotion can be judged by comparing them with threshold values.

screens.title: After changing the prompt, the quality dropped sharply, and I was unable to prevent it.
screens.lead: First, let's examine the process where a single deployment reveals an issue on Monday after passing through the weekend. Please refer to the timeline and quality line in the diagram together.

visual.alt: Friday release, weekend, Monday timeline of user complaints together with a declining quality metric line.
labels: Friday afternoon: Modify prompt by one line, then deploy operationally
No gate for verifying quality standards

paragraphs: On Friday afternoon, I modified one line of the prompt and immediately deployed it to production. The code ran normally and passed all tests. The deployment pipeline issued no warnings and quietly passed through the weekend.

On Monday, user dissatisfaction accumulated, and a significant drop in response quality metrics was confirmed. While rollback is possible, many users already received low-quality responses during the weekend.

What was missing? While there was a mechanism to verify that code was functioning, there was no gate to prevent changes that did not meet quality standards. This lesson covers release design that incorporates quality gates and scorers, ensuring that promotion itself does not occur if quality falls below the required threshold.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: Is it the same to say that the code works correctly and that the response quality exceeds the standard? This course distinguishes how these two steps differ within the pipeline.

screens.outro: First, let's recall what quality standards are in place in our current release.

screens.title: Are there any quality criteria that must be met before deployment?
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts are displayed. Since you haven't entered an answer, please first recall our release procedure and then try it.

items.prompt: Is this criterion stated numerically, or determined by the discretion of the responsible party?
items.answer: If quality standards depend solely on an individual's judgment, the standards may vary when personnel change or become busy. The standard must be expressed numerically—such as accuracy must be 0.80 or higher—to ensure consistent application each time. This number is the threshold for this course.

items.prompt: Is the step to verify the criteria executed automatically?
items.answer: The step where a person visually reviews and makes judgments about results is easily skipped during a busy Friday afternoon. Evaluation must run automatically within the pipeline, and whether the next stage is executed must be determined to ensure proper gatekeeping.

items.prompt: Who and how will know if the standard is not met?
items.answer: If the root cause is not communicated to anyone, even if deployment is halted, there will be no one to fix it. After an evaluation task fails, you must be able to view per-item results to identify where the evaluation value dropped, so that you can correct the issue and retry.

screens.outro: Now that I've recalled the desired form, I'll organize the core terminology required to establish the evaluation gate.

screens.title: Evaluation gate and scorer, threshold
screens.lead: The following flashcards explain five core concepts that establish the evaluation gate. Select a card to flip it over. Use the right arrow to advance to the next card.

visual.alt: Flowchart involving evaluation data, app execution, scorer scoring, and threshold comparison.

cards.back: This is a gate that code must pass through before being promoted to the next environment. Instead of asking whether the code runs, it evaluates whether the response quality exceeds the standard. It is designed to run automatically and determine whether to proceed to the next stage based on the results.

This process involves running an app with predefined input bundles and evaluating the outputs. Since the same input bundles are used each time, results before and after changes can be compared under consistent criteria. Snowflake's AI Observability also provides a feature that numerically evaluates response quality through bulk assessment of datasets.

A scoring function or evaluation model that takes an output and returns a score or judgment of pass/fail. Each scorer has a different perspective. For example, multiple scorers can be defined to evaluate accuracy, relevance, and safety separately.

This is the threshold that the value must exceed to pass. It must be specified numerically. Accuracy can be set separately for each scorer, such as 0.80 for precision and 0.95 for safety, and the threshold should be higher for perspectives with higher risk.

If the evaluation result falls below the threshold, the next step will not be executed. If any single scorer fails to meet the threshold, the evaluation task will end in a failure state, and deployment will not proceed to operations.

screens.outro: We've organized the terminology; now let's examine where this gateway fits within the deployment flow.

screens.title: Gate position in the bundle deployment flow
screens.lead: Select the following arrow to verify at which stage between the lifecycle phases of the bundle the evaluation gate enters.

visual.alt: A flow that progresses through create, develop, validate, evaluate gate between validate and deploy, and then deploy, run stages.

steps.title: What is a bundle?
steps.body: Declarative Automation Bundles allow defining Databricks resources such as jobs, pipelines, serving endpoints, MLflow experiments, and registered models in code, and deploying them as a single bundle. Configuration is written in YAML format and validated, deployed, and executed using the Databricks CLI. This approach enables source control, code reviews, and CI/CD practices in data and AI projects.

steps.title: Lifecycle: Creation and Development
steps.body: The lifecycle of a bundle follows the order of creation, local development, validation, deployment, execution, and deletion. First, create a bundle skeleton either through a template or by direct construction, then develop it locally with target environment and resource configurations and source files.

steps.title: validate: checks only the format
steps.body: The validation stage verifies bundle configurations and resource definitions against the schema of the target object. It determines whether the bundle is in a state ready for deployment to Databricks. Response quality is not assessed at this stage. Passing validation only means that the configuration conforms to the required format.

steps.title: deploy: raises the environment
steps.body: Deployment is typically initiated by verifying in a developer's personal development workspace, and then proceeds sequentially to staging and production environments. The target environment to be deployed is specified using the `-t` option. Since the same bundle is deployed to different targets across environments, there is structurally built-in opportunity to verify during the staging phase.

steps.title: Insert the evaluation gate
steps.body: You can define the evaluation task as a bundle resource and configure it to run first in staging, where it must pass evaluation before proceeding to operational deployment. The gate is placed between validate and operational deploy, i.e., at the staging run stage.

steps.title: Category: Verification is about form; gates are about quality
steps.body: The key distinction is this: verification checks the format of the configuration, while evaluation gates assess the quality of the response. The two are not interchangeable, so both must be present in the pipeline. A pipeline containing only format validation failed to prevent the Friday deployment of the initial scene.

screens.outro: Having verified the gate's location, let's now examine a case where actual evaluation results are used to prevent operational deployment.

screens.title: Case Explanation: Stop bundle deployment when the evaluation value is below the threshold
screens.lead: The instructor walks through a step-by-step example of evaluating a bundle with modified prompts in staging. Select the next arrow to follow the process of comparing evaluation values against thresholds and observe where deployment is halted.

visual.alt: A bar chart comparing the evaluation values of accuracy and safety against each individual's threshold line, illustrating the pipeline halting when accuracy is not met.

steps.title: Scenario: Set the threshold and deploy to staging.
steps.body: We deployed the bundle to staging with a modified prompt, and evaluation will proceed immediately. The thresholds were set at accuracy of 0.80 and safety of 0.95. Safety was prioritized at a higher level because safety issues have a greater impact on users and the organization.

steps.title: Step 1 validation passed
steps.body: `databricks bundle validate -t staging` completed without issues. The configuration format is correct. However, this is not a quality assurance. If you solely rely on this result and proceed to operational deployment, the same issue as the initial scene will occur.

steps.title: Stage 2 staging assessment
steps.body: The evaluation process runs the app on the entire predefined input batch, and for each output, accuracy scorers and safety scorers assess the results. The system collects the evaluation scores for each scorer. To ensure the average is meaningful, the entire evaluation dataset must be used, not just a subset of inputs.

steps.title: Step 3: Read Result
steps.body: The accuracy average is 0.71, falling short of the threshold of 0.80. Safety exceeds the threshold of 0.95 at 0.97. Because thresholds were evaluated separately by scorer rather than being averaged together, the high safety score does not mask any accuracy issues.

steps.title: Step 4 Block
steps.body: If any single threshold is below the critical value, the evaluation task fails and the operational `deploy` stage does not execute. This is because the pipeline is designed such that the outcome of the evaluation task determines whether the next stage proceeds, rather than relying on human visual judgment.

steps.title: Step 5: Follow up - Fix and repeat the same procedure
steps.body: Reports per-item results showing that the evaluation score decreased, and modifies the prompt accordingly. Re-runs the same procedure with the revised bundle—namely, staging deployment, evaluation, and threshold comparison. This time, when both scorers exceed the threshold, the operational deployment proceeds.

steps.title: Conclusion: The Friday change is halted before it impacts operations.
steps.body: The Friday change in the initial scene halts at staging evaluation and does not affect users. For the same change, if a gate exists, the issue becomes visible as a Friday evaluation failure instead of a Monday dissatisfaction. The gate does not create issues; rather, it makes issues visible before they reach operations.

screens.outro: Having completed the example, I will now summarize the core concepts.

screens.title: Key Takeaway: Evaluation is the gateway to promotion.
screens.lead: Organize the course content into a single release design. Review it by recalling the Friday deployment of the first scene.

paragraphs: Evaluation is the gateway to promotion. An app is run with predefined input bundles, the scorer assesses the output, and thresholds are established to define the passing line. When the scorer separately defines thresholds for different perspectives—such as accuracy, relevance, and safety—no issue in one perspective is obscured by a strength in another.

Validation and gate checks perform different verifications. Validation confirms only that the configuration matches the schema in terms of format, while the evaluation gate checks the quality of the response. Even if the format is correct, response quality is not guaranteed, so both checks are necessary.

Gates must execute automatically. The evaluation is first run in staging; if thresholds are not met, the evaluation task fails, preventing the operations deployment stage from proceeding. The reasons for non-compliance are verified per item, and after corrections, the same process is rerun. As long as this sequence is part of the pipeline, even a single-line change made on a Friday afternoon will be reviewed against the same criteria. The greatest value of gates lies in the fact that they are not influenced by personnel mood or schedule.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Thresholds are specified numerically and are compared separately for each scorer. By default, promotion is not granted if any scorer fails to meet the threshold.

checks.intro: Just learned distinction to verify. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: The bundle validation has passed. What can we infer from this result?
options: Response quality has exceeded the threshold
checks.explain: validate only confirms that the settings match the schema. Quality is checked separately by the quality gate.

wrong.0: Quality judgment is handled by the scorer of the evaluation task and the threshold.
wrong.2: Passing format checks does not guarantee quality, and thus is unrelated to operational safety.
wrong.3: The scorer runs during the evaluation task and is unrelated to validation.

checks.intro: Please follow the procedure in order. Results are not recorded.
checks.q: Review the flow of blocking operational deployments with evaluation gates in the correct order.
items: Apply a scorer to all evaluation data to collect the results.
Compares the result with the threshold value
If not met, the evaluation task fails and the operational deploy is not executed.
checks.explain: It is designed to evaluate during staging, compare the result against a threshold, and if the threshold is not met, prevent the next step from being executed.

glossary.def: This is a gateway that allows progression to the next environment only after passing quality assessment.
A function or evaluation model that grades one output or determines whether it passes or fails.
This is a threshold indicating acceptance criteria; it is a number meaning that the value must be equal to or greater than this threshold to pass.
When the evaluation result falls short of the criteria, deployment to the next stage will not be executed.
This is a unit that bundles Databricks resources and configurations into code for deployment across multiple environments.

misconceptions.myth: It is safe to deploy once it passes validation.
misconceptions.fact: validate only checks whether the setting matches the schema. Response quality is evaluated by the quality gate.

misconceptions.myth: Just raise the average evaluation score.
misconceptions.fact: The threshold should be separately defined for each scorer, and the process should be blocked if any threshold is not met. The average can sometimes view a problem from one perspective as an advantage from another perspective.

misconceptions.myth: The gate is the stage where a person visually observes the result and makes a judgment.
misconceptions.fact: The gate is automatically executed, and its design determines whether the next stage is executed based on the result. If left to human judgment, it might be skipped during busy periods.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Evaluation is the gateway to promotion.
The scorer evaluates the output and determines the threshold to set the passing line.
validate checks the configuration format, while the evaluation gate checks the response quality.
If the threshold is not met, the evaluation fails and the operational deployment stage is not executed.

closing.reflection: In my release process, where is the gate that automatically halts changes that don't meet quality standards, and what is that threshold number?
